articles.summary: arXiv:2409.09045v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: "Silicon samples" based on large language models (LLMs) have been argued to serve as efficient alternatives to surveys of humans, assuming that their training data includes information on human attitudes and behavior. articles.title: Prompt Engineer: Analyzing Hard and Soft Skill Requirements in the AI Job Market
articles.summary: arXiv:2506.00058v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has prompted speculation about a new job role: the prompt engineer. However, empirical evidence on how common such positions are and what skills employers expect of them remains scarce. In this paper, we present a data-driven analysis of a snapshot of LinkedIn job postings for data and AI roles taken in April 2025, after LLMs had entered everyday work but before LLM-based agents became widely adopted. articles.title: Frontier Open-Weight AI Risk Management Framework
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28082v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Open-weight models advance transparency, research, and innovation, and spread the benefits of AI more widely. They also carry distinct risks. A release cannot be undone, safeguards can be removed through fine-tuning, and no single party can monitor use or withdraw the model. Managing these risks therefore requires an approach tailored to open release. This framework addresses the governance challenge at the heart of that choice. articles.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate participants in social experiments. Existing research has primarily focused on aligning social knowledge and isolated responses, while overlooking whether simulations can reproduce the collective effects of social interventions. articles.title: Consumer Search and Social Learning in Agentic Markets
articles.summary: arXiv:2603.25893v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by agentic markets -- where AI tools facilitate search -- we propose a model of consumer search and market-wide learning. A sequence of consumers engage in costly search to acquire progressively refined signals of product fit prior to purchase. The market observes acquired signals and post-transaction feedback thereby impacting future searches.
